title: Quotient of a power-series ring by part of a parameter system
statement: Let $S$ be either $K[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ for a field $K$, or $\Lambda[[X_1,\ldots,X_n]]$ for a Cohen ring $\Lambda$ with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], with its maximal ideal and power-series structure [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. If $z_1,\ldots,z_r\in S$ extend to a regular system of parameters of $S$ (a minimal generating set of the maximal ideal of the regular local ring $S$ [def-weil-regular-scheme], and in the Cohen case this system can be chosen to contain $p$ apart from the $z_i$), then $S/(z_1,\ldots,z_r)$ is isomorphic as a local ring to a power-series ring in the remaining $n-r$ variables over $K$, respectively over $\Lambda$, with the images of the other chosen parameters as variables. In the Cohen case $p$ retains its role as the coefficient-ring parameter.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NM (lemma-quotient-power-series-ring-over-Cohen), clauses (2) and (4) and their proof

proof.text: Use the regular-complete power-series theorem to compute dimension n over the field and n+1 over the Cohen ring. Comparing with the length clause of the displayed regular parameter system proves length(z)+length(y)=n in either case, and hence the required parameter bounds.

Apply the full-coordinate equivalence for t=z++y in the field case, and for C(p)::t in the Cohen case. These proved equivalences fix coefficients and send each variable to the corresponding entry of t.

In the coordinate source let I be spanned by the first length(z) variables, and J the ideal spanned by z in the target. The variable values of the coordinate equivalence and list append indexing show J=map(I). Apply quotient_first_variables_equiv and rename the surviving subtype of indices to Fin length(y). Transport that quotient along Ideal.quotientEquivAlg. Check surviving variable values by applying the deletion equivalence to quotient representatives. An algebra equivalence reflects units via its inverse, proving IsLocalHom. Algebra compatibility gives the displayed equality for C(p). This explicit helper works for every commutative coefficient ring and includes empty z, empty y and zero variables.
